### Load data
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

billboard <- read_csv(file.choose()) |>
  filter(
    !Song %in% c(
      "All I Want for Christmas Is You",
      "Last Christmas",
      "Jingle Bell Rock",
      "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree",
      "Feliz Navidad",
      "White Christmas",
      "It's the Most Wonderful Time of the Year",
      "The Christmas Song",
      "Sleigh Ride",
      "A Holly Jolly Christmas"
    )
  )

glimpse(billboard)
```
```{r}
library(lubridate)

charts <- billboard |>
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date)) |>
  filter(!is.na(Date))

data_start <- min(charts$Date)
data_end <- max(charts$Date)

# Find each song's first chart appearance.
song_debuts <- charts |>
  group_by(Song, Artist) |>
  summarise(
    debut_date = min(Date),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(first_year_end = debut_date %m+% years(1))

# Keep songs whose first year is covered by the dataset.
# Songs on the first chart date may have debuted earlier.
eligible_songs <- song_debuts |>
  filter(
    debut_date > data_start,
    first_year_end <= data_end
  )

# Keep chart appearances before each song's one-year anniversary.
first_year_appearances <- charts |>
  inner_join(eligible_songs, by = c("Song", "Artist")) |>
  filter(Date >= debut_date, Date < first_year_end)

# Calculate first-year chart performance for each song.
song_first_year <- first_year_appearances |>
  group_by(Song, Artist, debut_date) |>
  summarise(
    first_year_weeks = n_distinct(Date),
    first_year_peak = if (all(is.na(Rank))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      min(Rank, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    debut_month = month(debut_date),
    summer_group = if_else(debut_month %in% c(6, 7, 8), "Summer", "Other"),
    first_year_top_10 = first_year_peak <= 10
  )
```


### Clean data
```{r}
billboard <- billboard |>
  rename(
    last_week = `Last Week`,
    peak_position = `Peak Position`,
    weeks_on_chart = `Weeks in Charts`
  )
```


### Song's debut date
```{r}
song_debuts <- billboard |>
  group_by(Song, Artist) |>
  summarise(
    debut_date = min(Date, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```



### Each song's peak position 
```{r}
song_peaks <- billboard |>
  group_by(Song, Artist) |>
  summarise(
    peak_position = min(Rank, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### How many weeks each song was on the chart
```{r}
song_weeks <- billboard |>
  group_by(Song, Artist) |>
  summarise(
    total_weeks = n()
  )
```
### Combine data sets
```{r}
song_summary <- song_debuts |>
  left_join(song_peaks, by = c("Song", "Artist")) |>
  left_join(song_weeks, by = c("Song", "Artist"))
```

### Find each song's debut month
```{r}
song_summary <- song_summary |>
  mutate(
    debut_month = month(debut_date)
  )
```
### Assign month to seasons 
```{r}
song_summary <- song_summary |>
  mutate(
    season = case_when(
      debut_month >= 6 & debut_month <= 8 ~ "Summer",
      debut_month >= 9 & debut_month <= 11 ~ "Fall",
      debut_month == 12 | debut_month <= 2 ~ "Winter",
      debut_month >= 3 & debut_month <= 5 ~ "Spring"
    )
  )
```


```{r}
billboard |>
  summarise(
    earliest_date = min(Date),
    latest_date = max(Date)
  )
```




##11/22 - trials, errors and lessons 

##Songs that debut in the summer reach better chart positions in their first year than songs that debut in other seasons

##songs that first made the list in the summer and compare those songs to ones that first debuted in other seasons *I defined a song's debut as the first week it appeared on the Billboard in my dataset. Songs that first appeared in june, july and august, were classified as summer debuts. 

```{r}
song_first_year |>
  group_by(summer_group) |>
  summarise(
    songs = n(),
    mean_weeks = mean(first_year_weeks),
    median_weeks = median(first_year_weeks),
    sd_weeks = sd(first_year_weeks),
    mean_peak = mean(first_year_peak, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_peak = median(first_year_peak, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```
## songs that debut in the summer reach higher chart positions than songs that debut in other seasons
```{r}
song_summary |>
  group_by(summer_group) |>
  summarise(
    songs = n(),
    mean_peak = mean(peak_position, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_peak = median(peak_position, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

##if songs that debut in the summer are more likely to be a top 10 song compared to songs that debut in other seasons.
```{r}

song_summary |>
  mutate(
    top_10 = if_else(peak_position <= 10, 1, 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(summer_group) |>
  summarise(
    songs = n(),
    top_10_songs = sum(top_10),
    percent_top_10 = mean(top_10) * 100
  )
```
##could compare songs that reached No. 1 across each season
```{r}
song_summary |>
  mutate(
    number_one = if_else(peak_position == 1, 1, 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(summer_group) |>
  summarise(
    songs = n(),
    number_one_songs = sum(number_one),
    percent_number_one = mean(number_one) * 100
  )
```
##I could look at the percentage of songs that stay on the chart for a least 20 weeks
```{r}
song_summary |>
  mutate(
    long_running = if_else(total_weeks >= 20, 1, 0)
  ) |>
  group_by(summer_group) |>
  summarise(
    songs = n(),
    long_running_songs = sum(long_running),
    percent_long_running = mean(long_running) * 100
  )
```
## see if the success of summer songs changed over time by grouping songs into the decade they debuted it and compare the amount of weeks they were on the chart and their peak positions.

```{r}
song_summary <- song_summary |>
  mutate(
    debut_year = lubridate::year(debut_date),
    decade = (debut_year %/% 10) * 10
  )


song_summary |>
  filter(debut_year >= 1958, debut_year < 2022) |>
  group_by(decade, summer_group) |>
  summarise(
    songs = n(),
    mean_weeks = mean(total_weeks, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_peak = mean(peak_position, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```

## Welch t-test to compare mean chart weeks between summer and other debut months 
```{r}
t.test(first_year_weeks ~ summer_group, data = song_first_year)
```

##how many songs reached top ten in summer vs other 
```{r}
top_10_counts <- song_first_year |>
  filter(!is.na(first_year_top_10)) |>
  group_by(summer_group) |>
  summarise(
    top_10_songs = sum(first_year_top_10),
    total_songs = n()
  )
```

##two proportion test: compare first year top 10 percentages 
```{r}
prop.test(
  x = top_10_counts$top_10_songs,
  n = top_10_counts$total_songs
)
```
